stem: Which pair has the same relationship as SENTENCE : PARAGRAPH?
hints: Several SENTENCES together make a PARAGRAPH. Which comes first in the stem: the smaller unit or the bigger one?
Make a bridge sentence that keeps the order: "Several sentences are grouped to form a paragraph."
Test each pair in the same order: "Several ___ are grouped to form a ___." Watch for a pair where the bigger unit comes first, and for people who only write or read.

solution.methodName: Make a bridge sentence, then test each choice

steps.action: Make a bridge sentence: "Several sentences are grouped to form a paragraph."
steps.why: The smaller unit (sentence) comes first and the bigger unit (paragraph) comes second.

steps.action: Test book : page. A book is made up of many pages, so the book is the bigger unit. Here the bigger unit comes first, the reverse of the stem.
Test author : essay. An author writes an essay. A writer is not a section of what they write.
Test reader : novel. A reader reads a novel. A reader is not a section of a novel.
Test stanza : poem. "Several stanzas are grouped to form a poem" is true.
steps.why: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, called a saknong in Filipino. A poem is divided into stanzas the way an essay is divided into paragraphs.

trapNotes.book : page: A book and its pages are a whole and its parts, like a paragraph and its sentences. But the bigger unit (book) comes first. The stem has the smaller unit first.
trapNotes.author : essay: An author writes an essay. This is a maker and what they make, not a part and whole.
trapNotes.reader : novel: A reader reads a novel. This is a person and what they use, not a part and whole.
